title: Damayanti
hook: the man who left her asks why she would choose again, and Damayanti has to answer

segments.voice: Yesterday, Damayanti's search: one question carried from court to court, and a test before she trusted. Your line was Damayanti. Did you send someone a small question only the two of you would get? Day one thousand three hundred forty-eight.

It's an odd first thing to say. Nala and Damayanti are face to face at last, in her father's house, after the forest, the cut cloth, the long separation. He still wears the changed, unlovely shape that has hidden him. And the first hard thing out of his mouth is a question for her: how could a faithful wife send out word that she'd choose another husband? The man who walked away is asking her to account for herself. Her third choice: what to say to that.
screen: `FACE TO FACE AT LAST.` → `HE ASKS THE HARD QUESTION.` → `HER THIRD CHOICE.`

segments.voice: First, notice what she does before he asks. When she sees him, the story says, she speaks to him with grief and with no softening: what kind of man leaves a sleeping wife alone in the forest? Who would do that, except Nala? She says it to his face. She doesn't pretend it didn't happen. And Nala doesn't defend himself as a man who was right. He tells her it wasn't fully him: Kali, the spirit of strife, had entered him, and was in him when he lost the kingdom and when he left her. Now Kali is gone. Then he asks his question about the second swayamvara. And Damayanti answers it straight. It was never real, she says. It was a way to bring him to Vidarbha, because only he could drive a king there in a single day. She swears to her faithfulness. And then the story brings in a witness. A voice comes from the sky, the wind itself speaking, and says she has kept faith with him the whole time. Look at the shape of the scene. Each of them has to be believed. He has to be believed that the man who left her was not all of him. She has to be believed that the swayamvara was a trap made of love. Neither gets to skip the hard part. She names the wound. He names what drove him. Then the truth is spoken out loud, and only after that does he put on the serpent's garment and become himself again. They hold each other. The story says that night they talk until morning, telling each other what happened in the forest. That's how this marriage is mended: with words, both ways.
screen: `SHE NAMES THE WOUND` · `HE NAMES WHAT DROVE HIM` · `THE WIND SAYS SHE KEPT FAITH` · `MENDED WITH WORDS, BOTH WAYS`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: both sides of a mending. Settle, and let the breath slow. Bring to mind a relationship where something was broken and has started to heal, or hasn't yet. Gently, without blame, let yourself name what hurt you. Then, just as gently, let yourself name what might have been driving the other person. Hold both at once, one on each breath. You don't need to decide anything. If you pray, you can pray for that mending. The bell holds the time.
Damayanti. The princess who chose the mortal, searched with a question, and mended her marriage by naming the wound out loud. Today's word.
Your line: Damayanti. Today, if there's something to mend, say one true sentence about it, and then listen to the other side. Day one thousand three hundred forty-eight.

howItsDone: Hindus know Nala and Damayanti's reunion from the Mahabharata's forest book; the sage tells it to Yudhishthira, who had also lost his kingdom at dice.

pairs: asked who would leave a sleeping wife
said Kali had been inside him
gave Nala back his own shape

myth: Damayanti pretended the forest never happened
she named it to his face: who leaves a sleeping wife alone?
the second swayamvara was a way to bring Nala home
only he could drive a king to Vidarbha in a single day.
Nala took back his own shape before the truth was spoken
only after the voice confirmed her faith did he put on the garment.

fork.setup: you're Damayanti. Nala stands before you at last and asks how you could announce a second swayamvara. what do you say?
options: the truth: it was only a way to bring you here.
turn it back on him and refuse to answer.
fork.reveal: she tells him it was a way to bring him home, and swears to her faithfulness. a voice from the sky confirms it.

original.note: Sanskrit: the princess of Vidarbha, daughter of King Bhima, whose story Brihadashva tells in the Mahabharata's forest book.

trapdoor: what you thought: Damayanti simply forgave him.
what it means: she named the wound first, he named what drove him, and the truth was spoken before anything was mended.
what a scholar hears: a voice from the sky vouches for her, and Nala takes back his own shape only after it does.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana (the reunion in Vidarbha: Damayanti's reproach; Nala on Kali; his question about the second swayamvara; her answer and oath; the wind's voice; Karkotaka's garment; the night of talk)

notes: Confirm the order of the reunion scene: Damayanti's reproach, Nala's explanation about Kali, his question about the swayamvara, her answer and oath, the Wind (Vayu) speaking from the sky, then Nala putting on the garment. Year 3 day 794 said only 'a voice from the sky'.
